import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Algebraic consequences of the Farrell–Jones conjecture

The assembly map in the Farrell–Jones conjecture is not yet available in Mathlib. This file
states two of its algebraic consequences using projective modules and matrices over group rings:
the vanishing of the reduced projective class group and the Bass conjecture for commutative
integral domains.

*Reference:*
- [BLR08] [arxiv/math.0703548](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0703548)
  **On the Farrell–Jones Conjecture and its applications**
  by *Arthur Bartels, Wolfgang Lück, Holger Reich*, J. Topol. 1 (2008), 57–86.
-/

namespace Arxiv.«math.0703548»

open scoped Classical in
/--
The value at the conjugacy class of `g` of the universal trace of a matrix over `R[G]`.

For each diagonal entry, this sums the coefficients of the elements conjugate to `g`. If the
matrix is idempotent, these values give the Hattori–Stallings rank of the projective module
represented by the matrix.
-/
noncomputable def matrixHattoriStallingsTraceAt {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {G : Type*} [Group G]
    {n : Type*} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n (MonoidAlgebra R G)) (g : G) : R :=
  ∑ i, (A i i).coeff.sum fun h r ↦ if IsConj h g then r else 0

/--
**Vanishing of the reduced projective class group for integral group rings.**

If `G` is torsion-free, that is, if its only element of finite order is `1`, then every finitely
generated projective module over `ℤ[G]` is stably free. This is the stable-freeness form of the
vanishing of $\widetilde K_0(\mathbb{Z}[G])$, which is the conclusion of Theorem 0.2 (ii) of
[BLR08] for the regular ring $\mathbb{Z}$. That theorem assumes the K-theoretic Farrell–Jones
conjecture for `G` with coefficients in `ℤ`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 16 19 20]
theorem projective_module_isStablyFree {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : ∀ g : G, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) M]
    [Module.Finite (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) M] [Module.Projective (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) M] :
    Module.IsStablyFree (MonoidAlgebra ℤ G) M := by
  sorry

/--
**Bass conjecture for commutative integral domains, in idempotent-matrix form.**

Let `A` be an idempotent matrix over `R[G]`. If the order of `g` is not invertible in `R`, then
the Hattori–Stallings trace of the projective module represented by `A` vanishes at the conjugacy
class of `g`. This includes every infinite-order `g`, whose `orderOf` is zero. This is
Conjecture 0.6 of [BLR08]. By Theorems 0.5 (ii) and 0.7 of [BLR08] it follows from the
Farrell–Jones conjecture with coefficients in every field of prime characteristic.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 16 19 20]
theorem bass_conjecture_integral_domain {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] {G : Type*}
    [Group G] {n : Type*} [Fintype n] (A : Matrix n n (MonoidAlgebra R G))
    (hA : A * A = A) (g : G) (hg : ¬IsUnit (orderOf g : R)) :
    matrixHattoriStallingsTraceAt A g = 0 := by
  sorry

end Arxiv.«math.0703548»

reformulations.difference: BLR08 Theorem 0.2 (ii) with R = ℤ is a conditional statement about K-theory: if a torsion-free group G satisfies the K-theoretic Farrell–Jones conjecture with coefficients in ℤ, then the change-of-rings map K_0(ℤ) → K_0(ℤG) is bijective, i.e. K̃_0(ℤG) = 0. The Lean drops the FJC hypothesis and states, for every torsion-free G (`∀ g, IsOfFinOrder g → g = 1`), that every finitely generated projective ℤG-module is `Module.IsStablyFree` (there is a finite free N with M × N free).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) K̃_0(ℤG) = coker(K_0(ℤ) → K_0(ℤG)). The map is always injective because the augmentation ℤG → ℤ is a retraction. So the map is bijective ⟺ K̃_0(ℤG) = 0 ⟺ every class [P] of a f.g. projective P equals k·[ℤG] for some integer k ⟺ P ⊕ ℤG^a ≅ ℤG^b for some a and b (because [P] = [Q] in K_0 iff P ⊕ ℤG^c ≅ Q ⊕ ℤG^c for some c) ⟺ P is stably free in Mathlib's sense. For the last step: if P × N is free with P and N finitely generated, then P × N ≅ ℤG^b because ℤG is nontrivial; conversely take N = ℤG^a. Using left rather than right modules does not matter, since ℤG ≅ ℤG^op via g ↦ g⁻¹. Letting M range over any universe is also harmless: f.g. modules are small, and IsStablyFree is invariant under ULift and Shrink. (2) Dropping the FJC hypothesis: FJC is conjectured for every group, so the unconditional statement is the open conjecture 'K̃_0(ℤG) = 0 for every torsion-free G'. This is the K̃_0 part of Lück–Reich's conjecture 'Vanishing of Low Dimensional K-Theory for Torsionfree Groups and Integral Coefficients', which BLR08 cites as the proof of Theorem 0.2. BLR08 also restates it right after the theorem: 'In particular we get for R = ℤ that ... K̃_0(ℤG) = 0 ... if the torsionfree group G satisfies the Farrell-Jones Conjecture with coefficient in ℤ.' The module docstring says the file states algebraic consequences of FJC, and the theorem docstring notes the FJC assumption explicitly.

reformulations.difference: BLR08 Conjecture 0.6 quantifies over finitely generated projective RG-modules P. Its hypothesis is 'the order |g| is infinite, or finite and not invertible in R', and its conclusion is HS_{RG}(P)((g)) = 0. The Lean instead quantifies over idempotent square matrices A over R[G], indexed by an arbitrary finite type. It uses the single hypothesis `¬IsUnit (orderOf g : R)`, and its conclusion is that the helper `matrixHattoriStallingsTraceAt A g` = Σ_i Σ_{h conjugate to g} (A i i)_h is 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: BLR08 (Section 'Bass Conjectures') defines HS_{RG}(P) := tr^u_{RG}(A) ∈ class_R(G). Here A ∈ M_n(RG) is any idempotent such that P is isomorphic to the image of right multiplication r_A, and tr^u sends Σ r_g g to Σ r_g (g), summed over the diagonal entries. The value at (g) is therefore Σ_i Σ_{h∈(g)} (A_ii)_h, which is exactly `matrixHattoriStallingsTraceAt A g`; I checked this in Lean on a 1×1 monomial matrix and on the identity matrix. Every idempotent A yields a f.g. projective module (the image of r_A is a direct summand of RG^n). Conversely, every f.g. projective P arises this way: the projection onto P inside P ⊕ Q ≅ RG^n is right multiplication by an idempotent matrix. Hence '∀ P' ⟺ '∀ idempotent A', and any finite index type is equivalent to Fin n. For the hypothesis: orderOf g = 0 when g has infinite order, and (0 : R) is not a unit in a domain; when g has finite order, orderOf g = |g|. So ¬IsUnit (orderOf g : R) ⟺ |g| = ∞ ∨ (|g| < ∞ ∧ |g| not invertible in R). I proved this equivalence in the scratch file. The case g = 1 is excluded automatically, as in the source.

review.notes:
I found no misformalizations.

- `projective_module_isStablyFree` states the open conjecture K̃_0(ℤG) = 0 for torsion-free G, in its equivalent stably-free form. BLR08 states this conclusion conditionally on FJC (Theorem 0.2 (ii), and the remark right after it). Lück–Reich, whom BLR08 cites for that theorem, poses it as a standalone conjecture. The formula `IsStablyFree` is the right target: "free" would be a different, stronger claim.
- `bass_conjecture_integral_domain` matches BLR08 Conjecture 0.6 exactly, using the paper's own idempotent-matrix definition of the Hattori–Stallings rank. The `orderOf` convention covers both the infinite-order and the finite-but-not-invertible cases.

Docstring checks:
- The references (Theorem 0.2 (ii), Conjecture 0.6, Theorems 0.5 (ii) and 0.7) match the arXiv numbering.
- The claim that Bass follows from FJC over all fields of prime characteristic is accurate: Theorem 0.5 (ii) gives the isomorphism I(G,F)[1/p], hence surjectivity after tensoring with ℚ, which is the hypothesis of Theorem 0.7.
- The J. Topol. reference is correct.

Status: both statements are `research open`. That is consistent with the literature: FJC is open in general with no known counterexamples, and so are its consequence K̃_0(ℤG) = 0 for torsion-free G and the Bass conjecture for integral domains. My arXiv search for very recent papers was blocked by rate limiting (HTTP 429). I know of no resolution of either problem, so I report no status issue.
